problemStatement.formal: IsSidon(A) := \forall a,b,c,d\in A,\ a+b=c+d\to (a=c\land b=d)\lor(a=d\land b=c); the greedy Sidon growth conjecture asks for |A\cap[1,N]| \gg N^{1/2-\varepsilon}, while the Lean file proves finite Sidon-set difference bounds.
problemStatement.plain: Keep the open greedy Sidon growth conjecture explicit while surfacing the verified Lean infrastructure: Sidon-set definitions, subset closure, injectivity of pair differences, and weak cardinality bounds for finite Sidon sets.
whyMatters: Sidon sets are central objects in additive combinatorics because their pair sums are essentially unique.
The greedy Sidon sequence growth lower bound is open, so the page should not read as if the conjecture is solved.
The formalized finite difference-set lemmas are still useful reusable infrastructure for the larger problem.

proven: `IsSidon`, `IsSidon'`, `isSidon_empty`, `isSidon_singleton`, `isSidon_pair`, and `IsSidon.subset` define and stabilize finite Sidon sets.
`IsSidon.diff_injective`, `sidon_pairDiff_injective`, `sidon_diffSet_card`, and `card_diffSet_eq` formalize the difference-set injectivity mechanism.
`greedySidon_strictMono` and `greedySidonSet_isSidon` expose the axiomatized greedy-sequence interface used for the conjectural part.
open: `greedySidonSeq`, `greedySidonSeq_strictMono`, and `greedySidonSeq_isSidon` are axioms; the asymptotic greedy Sidon lower bound remains an open conjecture.
knownResults.goal: Separate the verified finite Sidon infrastructure from the axiom-backed greedy sequence and unsolved growth conjecture.
